title: What If a Rogue Star Flew Through Our Solar System?

scenes.text: What if a rogue star flew through our solar system? Earth might not stay put.
Astronomers ran 12,000 simulations, each adding one passing star to the eight planets.
In over 95 percent of runs, every planet survived, though some orbits shifted.
Earth hit another planet in under half a percent of runs, and the Sun in about a quarter percent.
In one run, Earth was flung to the Oort Cloud, over a thousand times farther out than Neptune.
Don't worry. A flyby that close happens about once every 100 billion years.

description:
What if a rogue star flew through our solar system?
In 12,000 simulations, most planets survived, but a few runs sent Earth far from the Sun.
What should we run through next?
